Articles

Start here

Get started with anovakit

One analysis from start to finish (Welch’s ANOVA on mtcars, then the same question with a covariate in anova_ancova()), and the arguments every function shares.

Choose an analysis

A decision guide: four questions about your data that lead to one of the eight functions, a table of common situations, and what each function is for.

One outcome, independent groups

Welch's ANOVA: comparing means when variances differ

A walkthrough of anova_welch(): the omnibus Welch test, pairwise Welch t tests, standardised mean differences that do not assume equal variances, and the three diagnostic plots.

Kruskal-Wallis: comparing groups by ranks

A walkthrough of anova_kw(): the Kruskal-Wallis test, epsilon squared, Dunn’s comparisons with the tie correction, missing and infinite values, and the optional diagnostics.

ANCOVA: comparing groups at the same value of a covariate

A walkthrough of anova_ancova() on the anorexia treatment data: the homogeneity-of-slopes test, simple slopes, covariate centring, adjusted marginal means and robust standard errors (vcov_type).

Repeated measures and several outcomes

Repeated measures ANOVA: the same subjects under several conditions

A walkthrough of anova_rm(): mixed designs, sphericity corrections, generalised eta squared, within-subject residual checks, incomplete subjects and repeated rows.

MANOVA: comparing groups on several responses at once

A walkthrough of anova_manova() on the iris measurements: the multivariate test, univariate follow-ups, canonical discriminant analysis, Box’s M and Mardia’s tests, MANCOVA and several grouping variables.

Binary, count and other outcomes

Binary outcomes: logistic regression with anova_bin()

A walkthrough of anova_bin() on the Berkeley admissions data: analysis of deviance, odds ratios, marginal probabilities, separation, frequency weights and robust standard errors.

Counts and rates: analysis of deviance with anova_count()

A walkthrough of anova_count() on the warpbreaks and insurance-claims data: Poisson or negative binomial, rate ratios, marginal rates, exposure offsets, groups with no events and frequency weights.

Any GLM family: analysis of deviance with anova_glm()

A walkthrough of anova_glm(): a two-way Gaussian ANOVA with Type II and Type III tests, and a Gamma model with a log link for a positive, right-skewed response, with its coefficient table, dispersion, ratios of means and robust standard errors.

Guides

Topics that cut across the functions.

Working with results: the anovakit_fit object

What every function returns, how to print, extract and reuse it, how to go further with emmeans and the fitted model, and how to report a result.

Diagnostics: what anovakit checks and what to do about it

Every assumption check the eight functions run, organised by what is being checked: how to read each one, a worked example that makes it fire, and the argument or function that helps when it fails. Also covers exact fits and the limits of numerical precision.

Plots and themes

Every ggplot2 figure the eight functions build, grouped by kind, with what to look for in each; then how to change them, set a theme for all of them, build your own from the result tables, combine and save them.

Weights and robust standard errors

How anova_bin(), anova_count() and anova_glm() read prior weights as frequencies, trials or sampling weights, what happens to zero weights, and where vcov_type’s robust covariance reaches and when it is not used.

Design choices

Why the defaults are what they are, which decisions a function makes for you and where it records them, and which settings can and cannot change a result.
